title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
keyIdea: Don't merge: cut both arrays so the left side has (m + n + 1) / 2 numbers, i from nums1 and j = leftSize − i from nums2. The cut is correct when left1 <= right2 and left2 <= right1. Binary search i on the shorter array; left1 > right2 → fewer from nums1, else more. Median = max(left1, left2) for an odd total, else (max of lefts + min of rights) / 2.

approaches.name: Merge, then take the middle
approaches.idea: Merge like merge sort into one array, then read the middle one or two values.
approaches.why: Simple, but the problem asks for O(log(m + n)).

approaches.name: Walk to the middle without storing
approaches.idea: Same merge order with two pointers, but only keep the last two values and stop at the middle.
approaches.why: No extra array, still linear time.

approaches.name: Binary search the partition
approaches.idea: i = how many numbers nums1 puts on the left (0…m), j = leftSize − i. Check left1 <= right2 && left2 <= right1; move i left if left1 > right2, else right.
approaches.why: Binary search over the shorter array's cut positions only.

quiz.q: Why only check left1 <= right2 and left2 <= right1?
options: Each array is sorted, so left1 <= right1 and left2 <= right2 are already true
The other checks are too slow

quiz.q: left1 > right2. Which way does i move?
options: Left (right = i − 1): nums1 gave too many numbers to the left side

quiz.q: Why binary search on the shorter array?
options: Fewer cut positions (O(log min(m, n))) and j = leftSize − i never goes negative
For an odd total the left side gets the extra number, so the median is max(left1, left2)
